option.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on some finite AW*-factor admits a bounded increasing sequence with constant positive quasitrace increments.
option.approach: Starting from a hypothetical witness, examine scaling, matrix amplification, and passage to corners to determine which other positive increment values can be obtained while preserving the absence of a least upper bound.

judge.reason: It makes the definite claim that the set is empty, which is exactly the answer in e1.

options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound. Consequently, the no-least-upper-bound requirement is impossible regardless of the quasitrace increments.
options.approach: Find and verify the precise monotone sequential completeness theorem for finite AW*-factors, checking that its hypotheses agree with the definition in the problem. Apply it directly to the sequence bounded above by 1.

options.counterfactual: A witness for one positive increment can be transformed into witnesses for every increment strictly below one half. Scaling, matrix amplification, and suitably chosen corners suffice when combined with a localization argument.
options.approach: Investigate whether a witness can be localized to a projection whose quasitrace is arbitrarily close to twice the increment. Renormalizing the quasitrace on such a corner would produce increments arbitrarily close to one half.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor is strictly order preserving: if 0≤x≤y and x≠y, then τ(x)<τ(y). This excludes the endpoint η=1/2 even without resolving existence for smaller increments.
options.approach: Prove strict order preservation from spectral comparison and faithfulness, taking care not to assume additivity on noncommuting elements. Apply it to the equal quasitrace values forced by an increment of one half.
